c.tagline: Reggae beats, resort luxury, turquoise Caribbean shores.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are usually negotiated or fixed before departure rather than metered; use licensed JUTA taxis (red PPV plates) for reliable, safer service, especially from the airport.

emergency.note: 911 also works as a general emergency number in many areas; Cornwall Regional Hospital in Montego Bay is the main public hospital for serious emergencies.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Rose Hall: Rose Hall Great House, Montego Bay

avoid.reason: Avoid inner-city areas (Flankers, Canterbury, Norwood); resort/Hip Strip safe; St James has had states of emergency

hood_desc: The lively Gloucester Avenue tourist strip lined with beachfront hotels, bars, restaurants, and craft markets facing Doctor's Cave Beach; best for first-timers who want to walk to the beach, shops, and nightlife.

An upscale resort corridor east of downtown dominated by luxury all-inclusive megaresorts, golf courses, and the historic Rose Hall Great House; suited to honeymooners and travelers wanting a self-contained resort escape.
A quieter, mostly residential and golf-course district minutes from the airport with mid-range hotels and villas; ideal for golfers, business travelers, and anyone prioritizing quick airport access.

The historic commercial heart of the city around Sam Sharpe Square, with markets, colonial-era buildings, and budget guesthouses; best for independent travelers wanting local culture and lower prices, though it's less beach-convenient.

water.note: Tap water is chlorinated but visitors are generally advised to use bottled water.

transit.pay: Fares on JUTC buses and shared route taxis are paid in cash directly to the driver or conductor, and exact change is appreciated. There's no tap card for visitors, and route taxi fares are sometimes negotiated or confirmed before boarding. Knutsford Express intercity coaches require an advance ticket purchased online or at the counter.
transit.hours: JUTC city buses run roughly 5:30am-9:30pm; shared route taxis operate later into the evening on main corridors, but reliable night transit is limited and licensed taxis are recommended after dark.
transit.note: Most visitors rely on resort shuttles, licensed JUTA taxis, or rental cars rather than public buses, which mainly serve local commuters and don't reliably reach resort areas.

places.name: Peppa's Cool Spot

landmarks: Doctor's Cave Beach
A legendary white-sand beach with crystal-clear turquoise water, famed since the 1900s for its supposed healing properties and still one of Jamaica's top swimming spots.
Rose Hall Great House
A restored 18th-century plantation mansion shrouded in the ghost legend of the 'White Witch of Rose Hall,' offering candlelit tours overlooking the Caribbean Sea.
Sam Sharpe Square
The historic heart of downtown Montego Bay, home to a bronze memorial honoring national hero Sam Sharpe and the old stone slave jail known as 'The Cage.'
Greenwood Great House
A beautifully preserved 18th-century estate once owned by relatives of poet Elizabeth Barrett Browning, filled with antique furnishings and rare musical instruments.
Hip Strip (Gloucester Avenue)
Montego Bay's buzzing beachfront strip of bars, souvenir shops, and live reggae music, packed with cruise passengers and locals every evening.
Cinnamon Hill Great House
A hilltop plantation great house with panoramic sea views, now part of a golf course once owned by musician Johnny Cash, popular for its colonial-era architecture.
Montego Bay Marine Park
A protected coral reef sanctuary just offshore, drawing snorkelers and divers eager to photograph vibrant reef fish and clear Caribbean waters.
Rocklands Bird Sanctuary
A tranquil hillside garden sanctuary where visitors hand-feed dozens of colorful Jamaican hummingbirds, a favorite spot for wildlife photographers.
Montego Bay Cruise Port
The bustling gateway to the city where towering cruise ships dock against a backdrop of green hills, marking many visitors' first iconic view of Jamaica.
St. James Parish Church
A stately Georgian-era stone church dating to 1782, notable for its cruciform design and historic monuments, standing as one of the oldest buildings in the city.

train.note: Jamaica has no scheduled passenger rail service - the island's railways closed to regular passengers in the 1990s. Travel is by coach, minibus or car.

bus.note: Jamaica is an island, so there are no international buses. For long-distance travel within Jamaica (Montego Bay to Kingston, Ocho Rios, Negril, etc.) the main scheduled coach operator is Knutsford Express (https://www.knutsfordexpress.com/).

ferry.note: No scheduled international passenger ferries serve Montego Bay or Jamaica - cruise ships call at the port but there is no regular passenger boat line to other countries or between Jamaican towns.

half.name: Dunn's River Falls
half.blurb: Jamaica's iconic terraced waterfall that visitors climb as it cascades toward the sea.

half.name: Negril Seven Mile Beach
half.blurb: Long stretch of white sand famed for turquoise water and legendary cliffside sunsets.

half.name: Blue Hole
half.blurb: Hidden series of turquoise pools and falls perfect for swimming and cliff jumping.

half.name: Mayfield Falls
half.blurb: Gentle river of natural pools and cascades winding through lush tropical rainforest.

half.name: Luminous Lagoon
half.blurb: Rare bioluminescent bay that glows an electric blue when the water is disturbed.
